prompt: Which correctly creates a fixed thread pool, submits 10 tasks, and shuts down gracefully?
choices: ExecutorService ex = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(4); for (int i=0;i<10;i++) ex.execute(() -> doWork()); ex.shutdown();
explanation: newFixedThreadPool(4) creates 4 threads. execute() submits each task. shutdown() stops accepting new tasks after all 10 are submitted and waits for them to complete. Option B runs all work on one thread serially. Option C: stop() is not a valid ExecutorService method. Option D: ThreadPool doesn't exist in standard Java.
